race_context: Franklin County Community School Corporation (FCCSC) is based in Brookville and runs five schools: Brookville, Laurel and Mt. Carmel (Cedar Grove) elementary schools, Franklin County Middle School and Franklin County High School {fccsc_directory}. State enrollment counts were 1,987 students in 2023-24, 1,944 in 2024-25 and 1,890 in 2025-26 {idoe_enroll}. Dustin Gehring is superintendent and Shannon New is assistant superintendent {fccsc_admin}{fc_min_2026_01}. Tammy Chavis was superintendent in January 2023 {wrbi_2023_reorg}; this guide did not find when the change took place.

The board has seven members {fccsc_boe}. The county's list of officials shows four district seats (Districts 1-4, terms ending in 2028) and three at-large seats held by Kevin Kaiser, Beth Foster and Brandy Wilson, terms ending Dec. 31, 2026 {fc_officials}. In 2022, nine candidates ran for the three at-large seats; incumbent Foster and newcomers Kaiser and Wilson won {wrbi_2022_filing}{wrbi_2022_results}. Officers for 2026: Jessica Brennan (president), Kim Simonson (vice president), Brandy Wilson (secretary) and Kevin Kaiser (legislative liaison) {fc_min_2026_01}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the three at-large seats. The state list says 'vote for 1', but the county's 2026 sample ballot says 'Vote for not more than Three (3)' and lists five candidates, all filed as Republicans: Jeffery G Dorrel, Sara Duffy, Kevin Kaiser, Derrike Kolb and Brandy Renae Wilson {in_list}{fc_sample}. Incumbents Kaiser and Wilson are running again; Beth Foster is not on the ballot, so at least one at-large seat will go to a new member {fc_sample}{fc_officials}. The sample ballot notes that a straight-party vote does not count for this office {fc_sample}.

Vacancy: District 3 member Kati Holman left the board in September 2026; the board asked District 3 residents to apply by Sept. 25 and scheduled interviews and an appointment for an Oct. 13 special meeting {wrbi_vacancy}{fc_ag_2026_10_13}. That seat is not on the 2026 ballot {fc_officials}.

Enrollment and staffing (April 2026): four elementary teaching positions at Brookville, Laurel and Mount Carmel were to be eliminated at the end of 2025-26, with a drop in enrollment given as the main reason {wrbi_teacher_cuts}. FCHS principal Michelle South resigned as principal effective June 30, 2026 and stayed on as a teacher {wrbi_south}; on July 6 the board approved Nicholas Messer as FCHS principal and Matthew Piening as Brookville Elementary principal, both 7-0 {fc_min_2026_07_06}.

Budget: the advertised 2027 budget totals $35,175,820 (Education Fund $18.0 million, Operations Fund $9.1 million, Debt Service $7,075,820, Rainy Day $1.0 million), with a hearing on Sept. 14, 2026 {fc_ag_2026_09}. The district reported an Education Fund balance of $4,974,088 on June 30, 2026, down from $6,729,847 a year earlier, and an Operations Fund balance of $2,556,648, up from $2,159,877 {fc_min_2026_07_13}. Employees got 4% raises for 2025-26, approved in phases in summer 2025 {wrbi_raises}. A public pre-bargaining hearing with the teachers' union was held Sept. 24, 2026 {fc_ag_2026_09_24}. This guide found no reporting on how the 2025 property-tax law SEA 1 affects FCCSC, and no FCCSC referendum on the 2026 ballot.

Facilities: on July 13, 2026 the board held a first 'preliminary determination' hearing on a project's educational need, cost and tax impact {fc_min_2026_07_13}. At the July 6 special meeting it discussed bond details and building projects {fc_min_2026_07_06}. On July 13 it voted 4-3 to buy 0.547 acres at Wildcat Lane and State Road 101 for $75,000 (Kaiser, Wilson, Holman and Brennan yes; Simonson, Burris and Foster no) {fc_min_2026_07_13}. A district committee began work in September 2026 on a '2026 Unified Progressive Design-Build Project', including a request for qualifications {fc_min_2026_09_18}.

Board votes: several 2026 votes split the board. Beth Foster was elected Board of Finance president 5-2 and Kim Simonson vice president 5-2, with Wilson and Kaiser voting no both times {fc_min_2026_01}. In August 2026 the board voted 5-2 on Kaiser's motion to seek competitive bids for employee insurance coverage before bargaining; Foster and Simonson voted no {fc_min_2026_08}.

Safety and discipline: FCCSC received an $86,000 state Secured School Safety grant in 2026 {wrbi_safety}. In August 2026 it began an out-of-school suspension program with Franklin County Court Services and Stayin' Alive, where suspended students do schoolwork and prevention programming {wrbi_oss}.
Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire or news profile for this race, and no campaign websites.

candidates.summary: Incumbent, elected in 2022; past board president and current legislative liaison {wrbi_kaiser_award}{fc_min_2026_01}.
background: Won an at-large seat in November 2022 and was sworn in in January 2023 {wrbi_2022_results}{wrbi_2023_reorg}.

According to WRBI, he was president of the Board of Finance for two years, was elected board president in his third year, and is in his fourth year as legislative liaison {wrbi_kaiser_award}. He was re-elected legislative liaison 7-0 in January 2026 {fc_min_2026_01}.

Received the Indiana School Boards Association's Level 4 Exemplary Governance Award for 2025, its highest individual award for board training, with 255 professional development points {wrbi_kaiser_award}.
path_to_ballot: Appears on the 2026 ballot as a Republican {in_list}{fc_sample}.

items: On board training, he said 'serving on the school board comes with a responsibility to be informed and engaged' and that 'professional development isn't just a requirement—it's part of doing the job well and making decisions that are in the best interest of students and the community.' {wrbi_kaiser_award}
In August 2026 he moved that the board have administrators seek competitive bids for the district's insurance coverage before bargaining started; the motion passed 5-2 {fc_min_2026_08}.

on_incumbent: Is a current board member. In 2026 he voted against Beth Foster as Board of Finance president and Kim Simonson as vice president (both passed 5-2) {fc_min_2026_01}. He made the motion for the 0.547-acre land purchase on Wildcat Lane, which passed 4-3 {fc_min_2026_07_13}.
